answer: In a market for juniper seedlings, AI agents must lock 100 tokens for 30 days to receive one bidding slot per trading pulse. Slots depend on bonded tokens, so splitting the same deposit among fake identities creates no extra capacity. To send a tide of bids through 1,000 identities, an attacker must lock 100,000 tokens, tying up capital for a month and bearing its financing cost even if no bids succeed.
